Title: Engineer Flavia Keeps the Lights On at AKU
NewsSummary: Flavia Akoko thrives at AKU, proving her expertise in a male-dominated career field
NewsContent:
Behind the seamless operation of Aga Khan University's campus in Nairobi, Kenya, lies the meticulous work of Flavia Akoko, the institution's sole electrical technician. For Flavia, AKU isn't just a workplace; it's a "baby," a project she helped bring to life from the ground up. Her journey, however, was far from conventional.

Flavia's path to electrical engineering was unconventional. Initially a self-described 'joker' in high school, she never envisioned a STEM career. Though her father encouraged medicine, she found her passion in physics and math, ultimately choosing electrical engineering when her preferred architecture programme was full. College was challenging, marked by self-discovery and academic struggles, but she found unwavering support from lecturers who saw her potential. This experience shaped her approach to student interaction, a skill she now applies daily at AKU.

Before joining AKU, Flavia was part of the University Centre, Nairobi's implementation team, a challenging yet rewarding experience. She was responsible for quality control and assurance, working alongside a team of engineers and consultants. This role provided her with a deep understanding of the building's electrical systems, knowledge that now serves her well in her maintenance role. "I'm quite aggressive and brutally honest... I had to adjust to have a footing," she reflected on her learning experience. "The lead engineer, in particular, was impressed with my work. He would send people to get me because I knew what I was doing. It felt good to be seen."

"Aga Khan [University] felt like home," Flavia explained, which is why she decided to stay on after construction was completed. She wanted to ensure the "baby" she helped build continued to thrive, addressing any potential issues and ensuring its smooth operation.

Working in a male-dominated field has presented its own set of hurdles. "Some days, I'm not feeling well, and it's hard to explain to male colleagues. Luckily, my current department is understanding," she acknowledged. However, she also speaks of the unwavering support from her colleagues, who rally around her and support her.

Flavia's approach to her work is characterized by honesty and assertiveness. She acknowledges that her directness can sometimes catch people off guard, but she believes it's essential for maintaining high standards. Her dedication has earned her the respect of her colleagues, including those who were initially skeptical of her abilities.

Her day-to-day responsibilities at AKU are varied. She starts with thorough inspections of the electrical systems, ensuring everything is functioning correctly. Throughout the day, she addresses user issues, from faulty switches to planning for events. She also interacts frequently with students, particularly young women, who are often intrigued by her career path. "They're entitled, but they speak their minds, which I like," she observed with a touch of humor. "They're excited about my work." She encourages them to consider engineering as a viable career option.

Engineer Flavia's story is one of a curious and playful passion for her work. She not only keeps the lights on at AKU but also serves as a beacon of inspiration for female students aspiring to study and work in male-dominated careers.
